decisions.title: Use pipeline pattern for document processing
decisions.context: The system processes documents through a sequence of stages: extraction, classification, field extraction, validation.
decisions.decision: Adopt the pipeline pattern as the foundation for the DocumentPipeline module.
decisions.consequences: Provides a structured flow and allows easy addition of new stages in the future.

decisions.title: Separate I/O from logic
decisions.context: File reading and index storage are external concerns that should not be mixed with pure business logic.
decisions.decision: Implement FileReader and IndexStore as io-shell components, with DocumentPipeline using extern portals.
decisions.consequences: Keeps Dafny code pure and verifiable, while I/O is handled in C#.

openRisks.mitigation: Design TextExtractor to be extensible and add format-specific adapters as needed.
openRisks.description: Support for various file formats (PDF, DOCX, etc.) may require additional parsing logic.

openRisks.mitigation: Keep validation rules in a separate configuration or use a rule engine.
openRisks.description: Business rules may change frequently, requiring updates to validation logic.

components.name: FileReader
components.internals: Implements file I/O using C# System.IO. Provides a method to read a file's content as a string.

testCases.name: Read existing file
testCases.description: Read a file that exists on disk
testCases.expectedBehavior: Returns non-empty string content of the file

testCases.name: Read missing file
testCases.description: Attempt to read a file that does not exist
testCases.expectedBehavior: Throws an exception or returns an error indicator

components.responsibility: Reads files from disk and returns raw content.

components.name: DocumentPipeline
components.internals: Uses the pipeline pattern with stages for text extraction, classification, field extraction, and validation. I/O operations are declared as extern portals and implemented by FileReader and IndexStore.

testCases.name: Process valid document
testCases.description: Process a document with known type and valid fields
testCases.expectedBehavior: Returns a result with classification, extracted fields, and validation status 'valid'

testCases.name: Process invalid document
testCases.description: Process a document that fails business rule validation
testCases.expectedBehavior: Returns a result with validation status 'invalid' and error details

testCases.name: Classify document type
testCases.description: Process a document and verify classification is correct
testCases.expectedBehavior: Returns the expected document type based on content

components.responsibility: Processes documents: extracts text, classifies document type, extracts key fields, validates data against business rules.

components.name: IndexStore
components.internals: Implements a searchable index using C# and a document database or search engine. Provides methods to store and query documents.

testCases.name: Store and retrieve document
testCases.description: Store a processed document result and search for it by a key

testCases.name: Search non-existent document
testCases.description: Search for a document that has not been stored

components.responsibility: Stores processed document results in a searchable index.

dataStores.name: SearchIndex
dataStores.schema: Document with fields: id, type, extractedFields, validationStatus

auth.details: Requires API key for write and query operations

systemContext: A document processing pipeline that reads files, extracts text, classifies documents by type, extracts key fields, validates data against business rules, and stores results in a searchable index.

qualityAttributes.target: Process a document in under 2 seconds
qualityAttributes.rationale: Pipeline should handle high throughput of documents
Search index must be consistently available

qualityAttributes.target: Modular design with clear separation of I/O and logic
qualityAttributes.rationale: Ease of updating business rules or adding new document types

deploymentTopology: Single server with file system access and a persistent search index.
